symbols.name: _branch_literals

symbols.name: _dispatch_chains
symbols.note: Finds flat if/elif chains inside a function; returns chains with at least _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES branches.

symbols.name: _DEAD_BRANCH
symbols.note: String constant: 'inside a branch that can never run (`if False:`)'.

symbols.name: _SUPPRESSED
symbols.note: String constant: 'inside a `try:` whose ImportError is swallowed'.

symbols.name: _is_never_true
symbols.note: Checks if test is a constant that is falsy (e.g., False, 0).

symbols.name: _catches_import_error
symbols.note: Checks if a try node has a handler that names ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError.

symbols.name: _split_imports
symbols.note: Splits import records into live and weak based on context (dead branches, suppressed try).

symbols.name: _import_records_of
symbols.note: Returns only live import records from a node by calling _split_imports(node)[0].

symbols.name: _toplevel_names

symbols.name: _module_level_bindings

claims.text: "Mutable scratch for one parsed module. Never escapes ``analyse``."
claims.why: The _Src class is defined here; whether it escapes analyse is determined by usage in analyse, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "String literals a branch condition selects on. Covers the two shapes real dispatch chains use: ``x == \"literal\"`` and ``x.startswith(\"/api/\")`` (web_api routes a prefix on several paths). A branch we cannot read contributes nothing rather than a guess."
claims.why: The code handles Compare with string constants on left and comparators, BoolOp recursively, and Call with startswith/endswith attribute and string args. Unrecognized shapes return empty list, contributing nothing.

claims.text: "A chain is only a command table when it is long enough (``_MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES``); shorter ones are ordinary conditionals and reporting them as subcommands would fabricate entry points."
claims.why: The code collects chains and only appends if len(chain) >= _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES, which is the stated threshold.

claims.text: "``if False:`` / ``if 0:`` -- a branch the interpreter deletes. Deliberately literal-only. Inferring that some NAME is falsy would make the walk guess, and a guess in this direction silently deletes real edges."
claims.why: The function returns True only for ast.Constant with falsy value; no inference about names.

claims.text: "Does this ``try`` swallow a failing import? Narrow on purpose: only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count. A bare ``except Exception`` around an import is usually a lazy-optional-dependency idiom too, but widening this rule reclassifies real edges on evidence that is not there."
claims.why: The code only checks for ast.Name or ast.Attribute with id/attr in _IMPORT_ERRORS; bare except Exception (type None) is skipped.

claims.text: "(live records, [(weak record, why)]) for one subtree. Structural descent rather than ``ast.walk`` because the whole point is the CONTEXT an import sits in: the same statement is evidence in one branch and not in another."
claims.why: The code uses recursive descent via ast.iter_child_nodes, not ast.walk, and handles dead branches and suppressed try contexts differently.

claims.text: "LIVE import records only. Weak ones are reachable only via :func:`_split_imports`, so no caller can pick them up by accident."
claims.why: The function returns _split_imports(node)[0], which is the live list; weak records are in the second element.

claims.text: "Names a module binds at import time. Descends one level into ``if`` and ``try`` because conditional definitions are ordinary in this codebase."
claims.why: The code descends into If, Try, With, AsyncWith with depth < 3, and also descends into handlers, which matches the description.

claims.text: "``from .projects import resolve_repo_root`` binds ``resolve_repo_root`` to the projects MODULE for reachability purposes: referencing that name inside a dispatch branch is a real dependency on that module, and it is how HTTP route handlers reach anything at all (they call ``hierarchy.hierarchy``, never ``import hierarchy`` inside the branch). MODULE LEVEL ONLY, and that restriction is load-bearing. cli.py's branches all write ``from .doctor import main as m`` / ``from .benchmark import main as m`` -- the SAME local name ``m`` in sixty different branches. Binding names from every scope made ``m`` resolve to all sixty modules, so every subcommand appeared to reach every other subcommand's target and the whole dispatch collapsed into one blob. A branch's own imports are handled separately, from that branch's own records."
claims.why: The function only iterates tree.body, which is module-level statements, and binds names from top-level Import and ImportFrom. It does not descend into branches.

claims.text: "True when the module body re-exports and does nothing else. Detected structurally, never guessed: no def, no class, no executable statement beyond imports, ``__all__`` and plain alias assignments. A shim is worth naming because it is the one module class where \"nothing reaches it\" is expected rather than alarming."
claims.why: The function is only partially shown; the logic to verify 'no def, no class' etc. is not fully visible in this chunk.

claims.text: "Covers the two shapes real dispatch chains use: ``x == \"literal\"`` and ``x.startswith(\"/api/\")``"
claims.why: The code handles Compare with string constants and Call with startswith/endswith attribute; both shapes are covered.

claims.text: "A branch we cannot read contributes nothing rather than a guess."
claims.why: If a test is not Compare, BoolOp, or a recognized Call, the function returns an empty list.

claims.text: "only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count"
claims.why: The code checks handler type names against _IMPORT_ERRORS exactly.

claims.text: "The else IS the live branch" (comment in _split_imports)
claims.why: In the dead-branch handling, the else branch is recursively processed without the 'why' argument, meaning it is treated as live (since 'why' is None or empty).

claims.text: "the handler's own import is the fallback that actually runs" (comment in _split_imports)
claims.why: The code recursively processes handler bodies with the same 'why' argument, making them live if 'why' is empty.

observations.what: In _split_imports, when a dead branch is encountered, the else branch is processed with the same 'why' as the parent, which could be empty, making it live. This matches the comment.
In _split_imports, when a suppressed try is encountered, the handler's imports are processed with the same 'why', making them live if 'why' was empty. This matches the comment.
The _shim_body function is only partially shown; the docstring claims it detects no def/class etc., but the implementation beyond the first check is not visible in this chunk.
_walk filters out directories in _IGNORE_DIRS, but _IGNORE_DIRS is not defined in this chunk; it may be defined elsewhere in the file.
